option_description: Attests that the network edge enforces default-deny inbound: only documented, allow-listed (proto, port, destination) tuples cross-referenced to an asset inventory are reachable from untrusted networks; no any/any/allow rule, no shadow public IP, no forgotten dev/debug port.
security_impact: References "Exploit of public-facing application" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when ingress_default_deny_enforced is false (ATT&CK T1190). A missing default-deny baseline is what turns an internal-only service vulnerability into an internet-exploitable one, because surface that should never have been reachable becomes the initial-access path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Architecture review of the edge firewall / cloud security-group ruleset.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented edge firewall / cloud security-group ruleset with an explicit deny-all baseline and a finite allow-list of (proto, port, destination) entries cross-referenced to an asset inventory; absence of any 'any/any/allow' rule.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1 (Firewalls and Firewall Policy)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run an external full-port scan against the organization's public IP range and compare open ports to the documented allow-list.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only documented service ports (e.g. 443, 25 on the mail relay) are open from the internet; no management ports (22, 3389, 5985, 8443-admin), DB ports (3306, 5432, 27017, 6379), nor file-share ports (445, 2049) reachable externally.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 Network Infrastructure Management

option_description: Attests that a Web Application Firewall (cloud WAF, ModSecurity + OWASP CRS, or equivalent) sits in front of every public-facing HTTP application in BLOCKING mode (not DetectionOnly / monitor-only) with anomaly scoring at sensible thresholds — a WAF in monitor-only is telemetry, not a control.
security_impact: References "Exploit of public-facing application" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when waf_active_blocking_on_public_web is false (ATT&CK T1190). When the WAF is monitor-only or absent, SQLi / XSS / deserialization / RCE payloads reach the origin and the perimeter offers no compensating filter against an unpatched application.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the ModSecurity engine mode from the WAF configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SecRuleEngine On (blocking). 'DetectionOnly' or 'Off' is insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP CRS / ModSecurity documentation

how_to_obtain.instruction: Send a known-malicious payload to a public endpoint and verify the WAF blocks it at the edge.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: WAF returns 403 (blocked). CRS default inbound anomaly threshold is 5; a single critical-severity match causes a block.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP CRS (crs-setup.conf.example — inbound_anomaly_score_threshold default 5)

option_description: Attests that remote workforce access uses a Zero-Trust Network Access broker or, at minimum, a VPN that enforces phishing-resistant MFA, AND that the tunnel exits into a segmented zone with per-application authorization — not onto a flat internal LAN with broad east-west reachability.
security_impact: References "External remote service compromise without MFA" — its sole OR-condition — firing when remote_access_via_ztna_or_mfa_vpn is false (ATT&CK T1133, T1078). Without MFA at the remote-access edge, stuffed / phished / infostealer-harvested credentials become initial access; without downstream segmentation, that initial access becomes the whole internal LAN.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the documented remote-access architecture and authentication policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented architecture shows MFA required on every remote-access authentication; tunnel exits into a segmented zone with per-application policy, not into the office LAN with broad east-west reachability.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1133 (External Remote Services — M1032 MFA, M1030 Network Segmentation)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect VPN/ZTNA authentication configuration and verify MFA assertions are present in successful-auth logs (vendor-specific).
how_to_obtain.command: # vendor-specific: show authentication config / verify MFA assertion in VPN logs
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPN/ZTNA logs show every successful authentication included an MFA factor (TOTP, FIDO2, push); no users carry MFA-bypass exemptions.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture

option_description: Attests that every internet-facing edge appliance (VPN gateway, NGFW, load balancer, mail gateway) is on a vendor-supported non-EOL firmware build, with no CISA KEV-listed CVE past its remediation deadline — typically 15 days for internet-facing KEV entries per CISA BOD 22-01.
security_impact: References "Unpatched edge-appliance KEV chain" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when edge_appliance_patched_within_sla is false (ATT&CK T1190, T1133, T1599). A mass-exploited n-day in a perimeter device (CVE-2024-3400 PAN-OS, CVE-2023-46805/CVE-2024-21887 Ivanti, CVE-2024-23113 FortiOS) gives the attacker a privileged position INSIDE the perimeter with no downstream control to defeat.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-reference the edge-appliance patch register against the CISA KEV catalog and vendor advisories.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Patch register shows every edge appliance is on a vendor-supported, non-EOL firmware; no entry in the CISA KEV catalog applies to a running version past its remediation deadline (CISA BOD 22-01 floor: 15 days for internet-facing KEV vulns for federal agencies; private orgs commonly adopt 14-30 day SLA).
how_to_obtain.source: CISA BOD 22-01 (Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query each edge appliance for its running firmware build (vendor-specific show-version / get-system-status / request-system-info).
how_to_obtain.command: # vendor-specific: show version / get system status / pan-os request system info
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Running build matches the vendor's currently-supported security release; CVE-2024-3400 (PAN-OS), CVE-2024-21887/CVE-2023-46805 (Ivanti CS), CVE-2024-23113 (FortiOS) are not applicable.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog

option_description: Attests that admin / management planes (firewall admin GUIs, hypervisor consoles, IPMI/BMC, cloud-provider admin APIs, Kubernetes API server, Jenkins, RDP/SSH jump hosts) bind only to the internal management VLAN and are not reachable from the public internet — admin access goes through a bastion or ZTNA tunnel.
security_impact: References "Unpatched edge-appliance KEV chain" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_reachable is false (ATT&CK T1190, T1133, T1599). Most weaponised edge-appliance CVEs (Ivanti CS, FortiOS, PAN-OS) are only exploitable because their management interfaces are publicly exposed; hiding the management plane reduces a critical RCE to a same-VLAN-only finding.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan the org's public IPs for the well-known admin ports of common edge appliances.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All admin/management ports closed or filtered from the public internet; admin access reachable only via the bastion/ZTNA tunnel.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 Safeguard 12.8 (Maintain Dedicated Computing Resources for All Administrative Work)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the operator runbook and per-appliance interface bindings for each edge device.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented operator runbook proves that admin UIs of edge appliances (Fortinet, Palo Alto, Ivanti, F5, Cisco) bind only to internal management VLAN, not the WAN interface.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 (Network Infrastructure Management)

option_description: Attests that volumetric (L3/L4) and application-layer (L7) DDoS protection exists upstream of the org's bandwidth bottleneck — a CDN / scrubbing provider / cloud-native DDoS service — so an attack exceeding link capacity does not saturate the link itself, plus a documented runbook for engaging the scrubber during an active flood.
security_impact: References "Network denial of service" — its sole OR-condition — firing when ddos_protection_in_place is false (ATT&CK T1498). When the flood exceeds the link capacity at the target, on-prem filtering cannot help — only upstream interception by ISP, CDN, or scrubbing services preserves availability.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the contract / config evidence for an upstream DDoS service and the documented engagement runbook.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Contract / config evidence of an upstream DDoS service (AWS Shield Advanced, Cloudflare, Akamai Prolexic, Azure DDoS Protection, GCP Cloud Armor) covering each public-facing entry point; runbook for engaging the scrubbing provider during an active flood.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 Network Denial of Service (M1037 Filter Network Traffic — upstream interception)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Resolve each public hostname and inspect response headers for CDN/scrubbing-provider markers (the attacker's traffic should be terminating at the provider, not the origin).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DNS resolves to a CDN/scrubbing provider's IP range (Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Akamai) rather than directly to the origin; response headers show provider markers (cf-ray, x-amz-cf-id).
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1498 mitigation guidance (provider solutions)

option_description: Attests that outbound traffic from internal networks is default-deny with an allowlist of legitimate destinations / FQDNs, and that client-side DNS-over-HTTPS to public resolvers (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) is blocked so corporate DNS inspection cannot be bypassed.
security_impact: References "Application-layer egress C2" — its sole OR-condition — firing when egress_default_deny_enforced is false (ATT&CK T1071). Without egress filtering, established footholds beacon out over HTTPS/DNS/SMTP to attacker C2 and exfiltrate data; application-layer C2 blends with legitimate traffic and can only be defeated at the destination by an FQDN allowlist.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From inside the internal segment, attempt to reach an arbitrary internet destination not on the allowlist.
how_to_obtain.command: # from inside the segment: curl -sS --max-time 5 https://<arbitrary-internet-host>/
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Arbitrary external destinations are blocked; only allowlisted FQDNs (package mirrors, vendor APIs, telemetry sinks) are reachable. DNS resolution for unlisted destinations does not succeed via the corporate resolver.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1071 Application Layer Protocol (M1037 Filter Network Traffic — egress)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the egress proxy / NGFW configuration and DNS-resolver policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Egress proxy / NGFW config shows default-deny outbound; documented allowlist of categories/FQDNs; DNS-over-HTTPS only to approved enterprise resolvers (no client-side DoH to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 bypassing inspection).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1 (default-deny firewall policy)

option_description: Attests that authoritative DNS for the org's domains is hardened: DNSSEC signed with a valid DS record at the parent zone, no dangling CNAMEs pointing to deprovisioned cloud resources (continuous subdomain-takeover monitoring), SPF -all / DKIM / DMARC p=reject published, and the registrar account has MFA plus a registrar-lock against social-engineered hijack.
security_impact: References "DNS hijack or subdomain takeover" — its sole OR-condition — firing when dns_hardened is false (ATT&CK T1584.002). Without DNSSEC, registrar MFA+lock, and dangling-CNAME monitoring, an attacker can serve content under the org's own domain — defeating TLS validation from the user's perspective.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify DNSSEC chain-of-trust by checking the AD flag on the SOA response and the DS record at the parent TLD.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AD flag set on the response; valid DS record present at the parent zone (proves DNSSEC chain-of-trust delegation, not just signing).
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 4033/4035 DNSSEC (canonical assessor procedure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Look up the SPF, DMARC, and DKIM TXT records published for the domain.
how_to_obtain.command: dig TXT <domain>; dig TXT _dmarc.<domain>; dig TXT default._domainkey.<domain>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: v=spf1 ... -all (or ~all) hard-fail SPF; v=DMARC1; p=reject (or p=quarantine) with rua= reporting; DKIM key published.
how_to_obtain.source: DMARC.org / RFC 7489

option_description: Attests that no object-storage bucket (S3, Azure Blob, GCS) or static-website endpoint is anonymously readable unless it is intentionally a public website asset, and that account-level public-access-block is enforced (S3 BlockPublic*=true, Azure allowBlobPublicAccess=false, GCS publicAccessPrevention=enforced).
security_impact: References "Cloud-object anonymous exposure" — its sole OR-condition — firing when cloud_objects_not_anonymously_public is false (ATT&CK T1530). The boundary class deliberately covers the SaaS-edge surface, not only the firewall edge: a public bucket holding sensitive data is exfil via a single unauthenticated HTTPS GET.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the account-level and per-bucket public-access-block configuration on each cloud provider.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-public-access-block --account-id <id> --bucket <bucket>; az storage account show -n <acct> --query 'allowBlobPublicAccess'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BlockPublicAcls=true, IgnorePublicAcls=true, BlockPublicPolicy=true, RestrictPublicBuckets=true on every bucket; Azure allowBlobPublicAccess=false. GCS bucket iamConfiguration.publicAccessPrevention=enforced.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 + vendor public-access-block reference

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to fetch a non-public object via its anonymous public URL without credentials.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 403 AccessDenied for any object not intended to be public. A 200 on a key holding non-public data is an exposure finding.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS S3 public-access-block reference

option_description: Attests that every perimeter ingress and egress (edge-firewall ALLOW/DENY events, VPN session opens, WAF block events, cloud VPC flow logs) is shipped to a central tamper-resistant log store separate from the audited devices, with at least 90 days of online retention.
security_impact: References "Unmonitored perimeter crossings" — its sole OR-condition — firing when perimeter_crossings_logged_and_centralized is false (ATT&CK T1562 Impair Defenses, T1070 Indicator Removal). Logs that live only on the edge device can be erased by an attacker who has just compromised that device — off-box centralisation per NIST AU-9(2) is the only integrity guarantee.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM for the last 24h of edge-firewall, VPN, and WAF events and confirm every boundary device is reporting.
how_to_obtain.command: # query SIEM for last 24h of edge firewall ALLOW/DENY events; VPN session-open events; WAF block events
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-empty event stream from every boundary device covering the last 24h, with retention >= 90 days online + >= 12 months total.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management (8.9 centralization, 8.10 retention >=90d)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the log-destination architecture stores events off-box on a physically different system with object-lock or equivalent integrity protection.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs stored off-box (SIEM / log-archive bucket with object lock) — a compromised edge device cannot erase its own flow records; integrity-protection per NIST AU-9(2) (physically different system).
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AU-9(2)
